Product Updates

What we shipped

Technology  •  July 2026

One of the less visible but most meaningful investments we made this month was in automated testing.

The team added comprehensive unit test coverage to three major pipeline components: the Profiler, the Scoring pipeline, and the Staging pipeline. Everything from patient profiling and gestational age logic to provider attribution, baby-matching, pregnancy and postpartum processing, and the core machine learning model now has automated tests running against it. Full coverage reports have been generated so the team can see exactly where we stand.

The part that makes this stick: those tests now run automatically on every deployment.

This doesn't show up in a client meeting, but it directly improves how reliably we can ship and how confidently we can catch issues early. It's the foundation that makes everything else more trustworthy.

Analytics  •  July 2026

Something significant is taking shape on the analytics side: the Clinical Intelligence Dashboard is moving from analysis into the hands of clinical leadership.

Medical Directors will have access to a clinical population overview, condition breakdowns across PCOS, endometriosis, hypertension, gestational diabetes, and more, a full outcomes dashboard tracking C-section rates, preterm birth, and all 10-pack metrics over time, and real-time care gap alerts showing exactly where they can still make an impact this visit or this week. Every view can be filtered at the affiliate and care center level, and care centers are ranked by total patient opportunity so attention goes where it matters most.

Beta is underway now through September 1, with broad rollout to all affiliates targeted for October 1.

Accolades

Spotlights & shoutouts

NameRoleRecognition
Maksim Akhmetshin Sr Testing Engineer

Maksim got the Databricks testing framework across the finish line this month. What started as a foundational investment in how we test our data pipelines is now fully operational, with comprehensive unit and integration test coverage running across the platform. The work Maksim put into this directly raises the bar for quality and confidence with every future release. Well deserved recognition for seeing it through.
Aaron Southern Sr Director of Engineering

Aaron quietly did a lot this month. On top of everything already on his plate, he completed the CI/CD work that gets tests running automatically every time a pull request is created, which means the team now catches issues at the earliest possible point before code ever makes it to production. He also kept the lights on across the platform without missing a beat. The kind of contribution that doesn't always get the visibility it deserves, but makes everything else run better.
Clayton Weymouth Analytics Manager

Clayton presented the Lucina Clinical Intelligence Dashboard to Medical Directors in Chicago this month, and by all accounts he did a great job. The presentation covered Growth Ventures, the business unit focus, and most importantly the rollout of clinical intelligence to Affiliates, work that has been a long time in the making. Seeing it come to fruition in such a tangible way, in a room full of Medical Directors, is a meaningful milestone. Clayton showed up and represented Lucina well. Well deserved recognition. 🎯
Lindsay's Process Corner

From the process desk

How to Submit a Product Feature Request

Have an idea for a new feature or enhancement? There is now a formal process for it.

Fill out the Product Feature Request Form with what you are requesting, where it would live in the product, and the business or client value it would deliver. Every submission goes to the Product Core Team for review at the weekly Heartbeat meeting, and the more context you provide, the faster it can be evaluated.

New Faces

Ashley Childers
Head of Product
Ashley is joining as Head of Product, based in Evergreen, CO with her two step sons, aged 11 and 13, and two cats and two dogs! She comes with a decade of experience in HealthTech from athena, Humana, and Headspace, scaling solutions that improve outcomes for both providers and patients. Ashley spends her weekends in the mountains, backpacking, backcountry skiing, teaching yoga, mountain biking or winning the fort building competitions with the boys on camping weekends.
